'''Jeffrey Hudson Schenker''' (born December 22, 1972){{r|loc}} is an American professor of mathematics and current chair of the mathematics department at [[Michigan State University]]. His research focuses on [[mathematical physics]], with particular emphasis on [[Anderson localization]], [[quantum mechanics|disordered quantum systems]], and [[statistical physics]].{{r|msu}}

==Early life and education==
Schenker grew up in [[Laramie, Wyoming]], and completed all of his undergraduate and master's education at the [[University of Wyoming]]. He was named a [[National Merit Scholarship|National Merit Scholar]] (1991–1995) and elected to [[Phi Beta Kappa]] in 1995.{{r|cv}} He earned a B.A. with honors in chemistry in 1995, a B.S. with honors in mathematics and a B.S. in physics in 1996, and an M.S. in [[applied mathematics]] in 1997.{{r|msu}}

He received his Ph.D. in mathematics in 2002 from [[Princeton University]], with the thesis ''Schrödinger Evolution: Localization Bounds and Adiabatic Theorems in the Absence of a Gap Condition'', written under the supervision of [[Michael Aizenman]].{{r|mg}} He held an NSF Graduate Fellowship from 1997 to 2000 during his doctoral studies.{{r|cv}}

==Career==
Schenker was an [[National Science Foundation|NSF]] Postdoctoral Fellow at the [[University of California, Irvine]] from 2002 to 2003,{{r|uci|nsfpostdoc}} a postdoctoral fellow at [[ETH Zürich]] from 2003 to 2005, and an NSF Postdoctoral Fellow and member at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] from 2005 to 2007.{{r|ias}} He joined [[Michigan State University]] as an [[assistant professor]] in 2007, was promoted to associate professor in 2010, and has been a full professor since 2016. He served as Director of Graduate Studies from 2017 to 2020 and has been Chair of Mathematics since 2022.{{r|msu}}

He has held visiting positions at the [[Isaac Newton Institute]], the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne#Schools & Colleges|Bernoulli Center]], the [[Institute for Advanced Study]],{{r|ias}} the [[Mittag-Leffler Institute]],{{r|mfi}} and [[Sorbonne Paris North University]].{{r|msu}}{{r|cv}}

Schenker's research centers on the rigorous mathematical analysis of physical systems subject to disorder or randomness. His work spans [[Anderson localization]] for random [[Schrödinger operator]]s, quantum diffusion in fluctuating media, ergodic quantum processes, and mathematical models of statistical physics. He has published more than 70 research papers and received sustained external funding from the [[National Science Foundation]], including a CAREER award.{{r|cv}}

==Awards and honors==
In 2019, Schenker was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Mathematical Society]] in the 2020 class of fellows.{{r|fams|fams2}}
